Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile and the onboarding plan. We have a follow-up ask from procurement: the budget committee is comfortable with a 24-month total commitment, but they want the first quarter billed at 40% of the committed run-rate as an accelerated onramp (we have a constrained budget in Q1). Looping you both in — Skyline (strategic healthcare prospect) is asking for a Q1 billing concession: 24-month commitment total, but 40% of committed run-rate billed in Q1 (vs our normal ramp profile). Procurement wants a one-page concession memo for their CFO and an explicit true-up/termination guardrail. Decision needed by EOB Mon Nov 15.

Key facts:
- ARR-equivalent economics over 24 months roughly intact if they adhere to true-up in Q2.
- Risk: front-loaded usage below expected could create revenue timing and margin pressure for first quarter.
- Upside: larger strategic logo in healthcare vertical + potential case study and marketplace listing.

Ask: Can we get senior clearance (VP/CFO) to approve a controlled Q1 billing concession with explicit conditions (true-up in Q2, minimum aggregate usage floor across 12 months, no early termination without cure window)? Marissa, can you draft a short internal memo for signoff that I can share with Sara if we get the green light? Karthik — prefer your read on commercial precedent and recommended guardrails.

Thanks,

Kimberly —

I support a narrowly scoped concession for Skyline provided we bake in hard guardrails. Proposed conditions:
1) Q1 billed at 40% as requested, but a binding true-up in Q2 to the committed monthly run-rate for months 4-24. Any shortfall in Q1 converts to a contractual right for Redwood to invoice the shortfall at the committed rate at the time of the true-up.
2) 12-month aggregate minimum: if aggregate usage across the first 12 months is below 65% of committed volume, they owe an adjusted catch-up amount (capped at X% of annualized committed spend).
3) No termination without 60-day cure window for non-payment or underconsumption tied to onboarding failures; we also require a customer success escalation plan and quarterly checkpoints.
4) Concession limited to this single SOW; any expansion will use standard ramp tables.

If legal and finance can sign off, I recommend we approve as a sales-led risk (with marissa tracking revenue recognition impact). Please escalate to aditya for VP/CFO clearance — given the nonstandard billability and potential short-term margin pressure we need explicit senior signoff.

-karthik
